name: Omi
description: Omi is a Sri Lankan partnership plain-trick game of the Whist type. Four players in fixed partnerships bid trumps after seeing only their first four cards, then receive four more. Play is counter-clockwise. The 20 unused cards (2-6) serve as scoring tokens; the first team to collect 10 tokens wins.

content.text: Omi is a Sri Lankan partnership plain-trick game of the Whist type. Four players in fixed partnerships bid trumps after seeing only their first four cards, then receive four more. Play is counter-clockwise. The 20 unused cards (2-6) serve as scoring tokens; the first team to collect 10 tokens wins.
Omi is a popular card game in Sri Lanka; in some regions it is known as Oombi. The name suggests a distant connection with Hombre, but little trace of that influence remains.
4 players in fixed partnerships; partners sit opposite (North-South vs East-West).
Standard 52-card pack; only 32 cards used (A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7). Rank A high to 7 low.
32 playing cards; 20 token cards (2-6 of each suit). One player holds black tokens (clubs, spades 2-6); an opponent holds red tokens (hearts, diamonds 2-6).

Dealer shuffles and offers cut to opponent on left. Dealer deals 4 cards to each player. Player to dealer's right announces trump (without consulting partner). Dealer then deals 4 more cards to each (8 total).

items.text: Announced Kapothi: To win 3 tokens for taking all 8 tricks, you must announce before the seventh trick that you intend to win all eight. If you then lose one of the last two tricks, you give 4 tokens to the opponents.
